(p-490)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah At-Tariq

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the sky and the Tariq (the night-comer)﴾

The original meaning of ṭarq (طرق) in the language is striking (الدق), and from it comes al-miṭraqah (المطرقة, the hammer). Therefore they called the one who comes at night ṭāriq, because he needs to knock on the door (طرق الباب).

Upon this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Like you, pregnant, and one who nurses, I came upon (طرقت) her at night, and I distracted her from the one with amulets, the weaned child."

That is, I came to her at night. And the saying of another:

"Do you not see me, whenever I come as a night-visitor (طارقا), I find in her a fragrance, even if she has not perfumed herself?"

And the saying of Jarir:

"The enchantress of hearts came to you at night (طرقتك), and this is not the time of visiting, so return in peace."

And in the hadith: "I seek refuge with You from the evil of the night-comers (طوارق) of the night and the day, except a night-comer (طارقا) who comes with good, O Most Merciful." So it is a term that applies generally to everything whose arrival is sudden, as if it comes in an unexpected state. However, here it is specified by what is explained after it in:

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you know what the knocker is?﴾ ﴿It is the piercing star.﴾

It has been said: it is that which pierces the devils at the time of eavesdropping (istiraq al-sam', stealing a hearing), as has passed in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever now listens will find a watching flame lying in wait for him﴾ [al-Jinn: 9]. Thus it would be general for every star.

It has also been said that it is specific. It was said: Zuhal (Saturn); it was said: al-Irrikh (Mars); it was said: al-Thurayya (the Pleiades), because when "the star" (al-najm) is used without qualification among the Arabs, what is meant by it is al-Thurayya.

This has already been mentioned by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, at the beginning of Surat "al-Najm".

(p-491) It has also been said: "al-thaqib" means the bright one, which pierces the darkness with its light. In this case it is general in genus, since all stars are bright.

Al-Qurtubi said: Sufyan said: everything in the Qur'an that reads "wa ma adraka" (and what will make you know), He has informed him of it; and everything about which He said "wa ma yudrika" (and what makes you know), He has not informed him of it.

In reality this is the prevailing pattern. "Wa ma adraka" has come thirteen times, and in all of them He informed him of it except one, which is in al-Haqqah: ﴿And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 3]. As for the rest, He informed him of them, and they are: ﴿And what will make you know what Saqar is? It spares not and leaves not﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 27–28].

In al-Mursalat: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Judgement is?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 14].

In al-Infitar: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Judgement is? Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgement is? The Day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul﴾ [al-Infitar: 17–19].

In al-Mutaffifin: ﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is? It is a written record﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 8–9].

In al-Balad: ﴿And what will make you know what the steep path is? It is freeing a neck﴾ [al-Balad: 12–13].

In al-Qadr: ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾ [al-Qadr: 2–3].

In al-Qari'ah: ﴿And what will make you know what the Crushing Calamity is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 3].

And also: ﴿Then his mother will be an abyss. And what will make you know what that is? A fiercely burning fire﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 9–11]. And in this surah: ﴿And what will make you know what the knocker is? It is the piercing star.﴾ All of these, He informed him of, except in al-Haqqah.

Note (tanbih):
It is noticed that all of these occur in short surahs, from al-Haqqah onward. As for "ma yudrika", it has come only three times: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Ahzab: 63]; in al-Ahzab; ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura: 17], in al-Shura; ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself﴾ [Abasa: 3], in Abasa wa Tawalla. In these, He did not explicitly inform him, except that in the third instance He may have informed him, since He said: ﴿Perhaps he would purify himself﴾. Although He did not state explicitly whether he purified himself or not, "perhaps" (la'alla) from Allah, exalted is He, indicates certainty, as is well known.

Another note (tanbih):
Many of the exegetes said: Allah swore by the sky and by the knocking star, because of the greatness of their matter and the vastness of their creation, as in His saying: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, that is great﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 75–76]; and because He swore by the star when it sets (hawa) [al-Najm: 1]. What has preceded from the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, is the preference that the "positions of the stars" (mawaqi' al-nujum) in ﴿And by the star when it sets﴾ [al-Najm: 1] refers only to the stars of the Qur'an, its being revealed in portions (munajjaman), and that its revelation through the Angel to the Prophet ﷺ is what is meant.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is over every soul a guardian.﴾

It has been said: "guardian" means one who keeps account of its deeds, recording them against it, as in His saying: ﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watchful observer, ready.﴾ [Qaf: 18]

And it has been said: "guardian" means a protector (ḥāris), as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For him there are successive [angels] before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of Allah.﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11] The context supports both meanings together, because His saying after it: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a fluid ejected﴾ ﴿emerging from between the backbone and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq: 5–7] indicates that during those stages he is under protection, [as in] His saying: ﴿in a firm lodging﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 13] at first.

And in a hadith: "Indeed Allah has appointed an angel over the womb..." and the hadith continues.

After he reaches the age of legal responsibility (sinn al-taklif), the pen runs over him and records his deeds, so there is no barrier to intending both meanings together. This is not the case of applying a homonym (mushtarak) to both of its meanings, because each of the two meanings has a referent (muta'alliq) specific to a time different from the other.

﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنْسانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ﴾

"Al-Insan" here is specific to the children of Adam and their descendants in general. It does not include Adam, Hawwa' (Eve), or 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, because the verse itself specifies what man was created from, namely in His saying, ﴿He was created from a gushing fluid﴾ ﴿that emerges from between the backbone and the ribs﴾.

(p-٤٩٣) The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained this verse at His saying, ﴿He created man from a drop of semen﴾ (al-Nahl: 4), in Surat al-Nahl, and in Surat al-Waqi'ah at His saying, ﴿Have you considered that which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ (al-Waqi'ah: 58-59). A reference to it was also made at His saying, ﴿Indeed, We created man from a mixed drop﴾ (al-Insan: 2), in Surat al-Dahr.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him.﴾ "Innahu" here means: indeed Allah is "able to return him." Regarding the pronoun in "rajʿihi" (His returning him), it has been said that it refers to the gushing water (al-ma' al-dafiq), meaning: indeed He, glorified is He, is able to return this water from where it came out, like the returning of milk to the udder, for example, and the returning of the child to the womb. This is related from ʿIkrimah and Mujahid.

It has also been said that it means "the return of the human being after death." Although the first view indicates [Allah's] power, and none is able to do that except Allah, the context contains indications that the intended meaning is the second, for several reasons:

The first: the returning of the water is not connected to any ruling or any other matter apart from establishing power, unlike the return of the human being after death, which is a matter of faith in the Resurrection (al-baʿth), and to which all the rulings of the Day of Judgment are connected.

The second: the Qur'an's mention of the first creation is evidence for the restoration after death, as in His saying, may He be exalted, in Ya-Sin: ﴿And he presents for Us a parable and forgets his creation.﴾ That is, from a gushing water: ﴿He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78–79], that is, ﴿from a gushing water﴾ ﴿emerging from between the backbone and the ribs.﴾

The third: that the first view requires an assumed governing verb (ʿamil) for ﴿the Day the secrets are examined﴾, such as "remember," for example, whereas in the second view the governing element is "la-qadir" (surely able), meaning: surely able to return him on the Day the secrets are examined.

Abu Hayyan transmitted from Ibn ʿAtiyyah his saying: "Everyone who opposed this only fled from the possibility that ‘la-qadir’ is the governing element of the adverbial phrase (al-zarf), because it would give the impression that His power to return him is restricted to that time. But by reflecting on the style of the Arabs, its permissibility is known, because He said: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him﴾ absolutely, first and last, and at every time; then He mentioned and specified among the times the most important time for the disbelievers, because it is the time of recompense and of reaching the punishment, as a warning against it." End of quotation.

Thus it becomes clear that the pronoun in "rajʿihi" refers to the human being, meaning: after his death, by resurrection, and that the governing element is "la-qadir."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 9:

His statement, may Allah have mercy on us and on him, the Most High: ﴿The Day when the secrets are tested﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah the Most High have mercy on us and on him, had already explained this when discussing His words, the Most High: ﴿There every soul will taste what it sent before﴾ [Yunus: 30], and he cited this verse there. The explicit statement about it will come in surah "al-'Adiyat" at His words, the Most High: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered﴾ ﴿and what is within the breasts is obtained﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 9-10]. He has here summarized the testing of the secrets.

Likewise, the Shaykh, may Allah the Most High have mercy on us and on him, summarized it by citing the verses.

The exegetes mentioned that what is meant by them is the trust of moral responsibility (taklif) in matters that none knows but Allah, and they gave as examples: guarding purity for prayer, the ritual bath from major impurity (ghusl al-janabah), observing the fast, and the like. Among them are the beliefs and the sincerity of faith or hypocrisy, we seek refuge in Allah.

And the sara'ir (secrets) are: everything that a person conceals, even in his dealings with people, as in the report: "The clever one is he who has a hidden store of secret good deeds with Allah," and His words: ﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it openly﴾ [al-Mulk: 13]. So sirr (secret) is the opposite of jahr (open declaration). Al-Ahwas said:

"There will remain for her, in the hidden depths of the heart and the inner self, a secret affection on the Day when the secrets are tested."

Abu Hayyan said: al-Hasan heard it and said: "How heedless he is of what is in the sky and the Tariq (surah)."

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 10:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So he will have no power, nor any helper﴾

They said: He has no power in himself because of his weakness. This is indicated by His words: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: "You have certainly come to Us as We created you the first time."﴾ [al-Kahf: 48].

And His words: ﴿Their eyes humbled, humiliation covering them﴾ [al-Qalam: 43], meaning: from weakness and intense fear. And he has no helper other than Him, as in His words: ﴿He had no group to help him against Allah, nor was he one who could defend himself﴾ [al-Kahf: 43].

(p-495) And His words: ﴿The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Infitar: 19].

By the sky, which returns (the rain), and by the earth, which splits (for growth).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the sky, which has returning (ar-raj'); and by the earth, which has cracking (as-sad')﴾. It was said: the "raj'" of the sky is the restoring of the light of the stars, the sun and the moon.

It was also said: "ar-raj'" refers to the angels, who carry back the deeds of the servants.

It was also said: "ar-raj'" refers to the rain and the provision of the servants. ﴿And by the earth, which has cracking﴾: it was said that it splits open to release the creatures on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that it splits open with vegetation.

What the Qur'an bears witness to is that the returning and the cracking are complementary between the sky and the earth: through rain and plants. As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let man look at his food. That We pour down water in abundance. Then We split the earth in splitting. And We cause the grain to grow therein, and grapes and herbage﴾ [Abasa: 24–28]. And Allah knows best.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾. Ibn Kathir said: Ibn 'Abbas said: it is true. Qatadah said the same. Others said: it is a just judgment. Al-Qurtubi said: it means the Qur'an, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood.

It has also been said: it refers to the threat mentioned earlier in this surah: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him﴾ ﴿on the day when the secrets are examined﴾ [al-Tariq: 8-9].

Abu Hayyan first said what al-Qurtubi said, then allowed that it may also refer to the second meaning, namely that the report about the return of man on the day when the secrets are examined is a decisive word. This is what the words of Ibn Jarir imply, and al-Naysaburi attributed it to al-Qaffal.

The context of the surah supports this second view, because the whole surah is devoted to establishing the power to resurrect and to restore man after annihilation. It contains three proofs of the resurrection:

The first: the heaven with its Tariq (the piercing star), because of the greatness of its creation and the greatness of its indication of power.

The second: the creation of man first from a gushing fluid, as in His saying: ﴿Say: He will give them life who originated them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79].

The third: the combination of His saying: ﴿By the heaven of the return﴾ ﴿and the earth of the splitting﴾, that is, the sending down of rain and the growth of plants, which is the giving of life to the earth after its death. It is therefore appropriate that the oath be sworn to confirm the reality of the resurrection.

What follows confirms this, namely the threat with a respite: ﴿Give them respite, a little while﴾. The Day of Resurrection has been called the Day of Judgment (al-Fasl), as in His saying: ﴿For what day were they postponed?﴾ ﴿For the Day of Judgment﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?﴾ ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat: 12-15].

Mentioning woe in that verse for the deniers corresponds to the respite granted to the disbelievers in this surah. If we connect the oath with what it is sworn to, the meaning becomes clearer and more evident, because the return of water after its disappearance through the fertilization of clouds anew corresponds to the return of man after his annihilation in the earth, and the splitting of the earth to bring forth plants is fitting for its splitting on the Day of Resurrection to bring forth the creatures. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot﴾ ﴿and I am plotting a plot﴾. The attribution of this action to Him, may He be exalted, [some] have said: it is of the type of reciprocal correspondence (al-muqabalah), like His saying: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, we are mockers﴾ ﴿Allah mocks at them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14-15]. In language it is like the saying of one who, when asked which food he wants while he is naked and wants clothing:

"They said: Choose a food, we will find you a dish. I said: Cook for me a robe and a shirt."

The early scholars (al-Salaf) agreed that this action is not attributed to Allah, may He be exalted, in an absolute manner, and it is not permissible to derive a name for Him from it. It is only used in correspondence with the actions of the servants, because outside of correspondence it is not fitting for Allah, may He be exalted. In the context of correspondence, it is of utmost knowledge, wisdom and power. The root meaning of kayd (plotting) is hastening toward a thing with strength.

Ibn Faris said in Mu'jam Maqayis al-Lughah: The Arabs sometimes use kayd to mean makr (scheming), and the Arabs sometimes call makr kayd. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Or do they intend a plot?﴾ [al-Tur: 42]. Accordingly, the kayd here is not explained, but if it means makr, then the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already given an explanation of part of it at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 54]; that their makr was their attempt to kill Isa, and Allah's makr was the casting of a likeness, i.e., He made Isa's likeness fall upon someone other than Isa.

His saying, may He be exalted, has also preceded: ﴿Those before them had already schemed, so Allah came at their structure from its foundations, and the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾ [al-Nahl: 26]. This is about the story of Nimrod, whose makr was building the tower to ascend to the heaven, and Allah's makr against them was to leave them until they ascended with the building; then Allah came at their structure from its foundations and demolished it upon them.

Likewise is the kayd here: they plot against Islam and the Muslims, wishing to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, while Allah plots against them through gradual leading on (istidraj) until the appointed time of their destruction comes. Its fulfillment occurred at Badr, when they went out in opposition to Allah and His Messenger, with arrogance and boasting. Allah's kayd against them was that He made the believers appear few in their eyes, until they became eager for fighting; and He sent rain upon the battlefield, while they were on soft sandy ground and the Muslims were on sand that became firm, so it was slippery for them and a firm footing for the believers. Then He sent down His angels to fight them. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 86, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them a little respite.﴾ The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in repelling the appearance of contradiction (in the passage), the following text: This respite mentioned here is contradicted by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], and the rest of the verse.

The answer: the respite is abrogated (mansukh) by the verses of the sword (ayat al-sayf). End of quotation.

This is what the words of al-Tabari imply, although he does not state it explicitly, and it is the explicit view of al-Qurtubi. Perhaps there is in the verse itself what indicates this, namely His saying: ﴿give them a little respite﴾; because "ruwaydan" means "a little," so He restricted the respite to a small amount, which suggests that the abrogation will come and that it is not final. And Allah knows best.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Repelling the Appearance of Contradiction Regarding the Verses of the Book):

Surah al-Tariq

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them a little respite.﴾

This respite mentioned here is contradicted by His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], and the rest of the verse.

The answer is that the respite is abrogated by the verses of the sword, and Allah knows best.
